solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some provided source of Latin poetry

indicators.note: some says only part of the next word is wanted, a run of letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain supplier furnished the raw material for Roman verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman poet who wrote the Metamorphoses is a prime fount of classical Latin verse.

clue.text: Maids serving King drink within six seconds

indicators.note: within says the king and drink pieces sit inside the six-and-seconds pair

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
R is Rex, Latin for king
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Housemaids serving the monarch a tipple in a matter of moments.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid in its old sense means a young unmarried woman, a chaste girl.

clue.text: Ate in study I'd set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up says the letters are read from the bottom upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom
I'd written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone had a meal in the study they had arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean took a meal; the past tense of eat matches the past tense of dine.

clue.text: Admen had styles personally crafted

indicators.note: styles as a verb means shapes or arranges, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Advertising men designing something they made with their own hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made by hand rather than machine is crafted personally by its maker.

clue.text: The girl's seeing the earl regularly

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A young woman is dating a nobleman on a steady basis.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a female, belonging to her, as in 'that girl's coat'.

clue.text: She has the latest snowman we built

indicators.note: built suggests something constructed out of parts, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A snowman we made, with a woman owning the newest one.
explanation.definitionFit: A female journalist is the woman who holds the most recent news.

clue.text: Older erratum corrected

indicators.note: corrected says the letters of the misprint need putting right, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An earlier misprint has now been fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: More mature means further along in years, so older.

clue.text: Amusing conclusion to repeated spin

indicators.note: conclusion to means the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over, to spin

explanation.surface: Something funny about the end of a twirl done over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll describes wry, quietly funny humour, so amusing is a synonym.

clue.text: Three of the fifteen best seats?

definitions.meaning: a rugby union side has fifteen players, and the three props and hooker forwards at the front of the scrum are its leading trio
in a theatre the seats nearest the stage are often thought the best

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a trio from a team of fifteen have the finest places.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen is a rugby union team; its front row is the two props and the hooker, three players in the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby's three front forwards and the theatre's foremost line of seating share the same phrase.

clue.text: Instrument in sack brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the word is turned to run the other way

parts.note: sack as a noun means plunder, booty taken by looting

explanation.surface: A device carried home in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement or device used for work, an instrument.

clue.text: Auditor's punished for discovery

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this is the version heard rather than written

parts.note: fined means penalised with a money charge, punished

explanation.surface: An accountant has been penalised for something they uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, but here it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is something valuable turned up, as in 'that antique was a real find'.

clue.text: Yellow clay rod somehow bearing weight

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the shuffled letters carry the weight letter inside them
somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Yellow clay formed into a rod somehow holding up a load.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal rearranges CLAY ROD to COARDLY; 'bearing' then puts W inside it. 'Yellow' looks like the colour of the clay but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for lacking courage, timid and fearful.

clue.text: Someone who arrives holding mike, with officer in charge?

indicators.note: holding says the first piece wraps round the following pieces

parts.note: a comer is one who comes, an arrival
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
and means together with

explanation.surface: A newcomer clutching a microphone, accompanied by the officer in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' is a radio code word for the letter M, not a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval or military rank given to an officer who leads, someone in command.

clue.text: Judge encounters advocate, finally, when returning

indicators.note: returning says the assembled letters are read back the other way

parts.note: meets means comes across, encounters

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A judge meets a barrister at last on the way back.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem as a verb can mean to consider or regard, to judge something to be so.

clue.text: On reflection, some felt it needed permit

indicators.note: On reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, a few people felt a licence was required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ELTITNE out of fELT IT NEEDed; 'On reflection' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to give someone the right or authority to do something, to allow.

clue.text: Month that ends too soon for girl

parts.note: Mar is the short form of March

indicators.note: ends too soon says the word stops before its final letter

explanation.surface: A calendar month that finishes early on a young woman's account.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so an example of a girl as crosswords often treat names.

clue.text: Game where the suspense comes at the end

definitions.text: Game where the suspense comes at the end

parts.words: Game where the suspense comes at the end
parts.note: a word-guessing pencil game ends with a stick figure drawn hanging; suspense also means being suspended

explanation.surface: A description of a pastime with a nail-biting finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspense puns on suspension: the drawn figure is left dangling from the gallows once the guesses run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper word game where wrong guesses build up a gallows drawing until the figure swings.

clue.text: Hold back from relaxation, then shower

parts.note: rest is relaxation, a break from effort
a shower is a short fall of rain

explanation.surface: Holding off from a break and then a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to keep in check, to hold someone or something back.

clue.text: Books are turning up inspirational source

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom upwards, so reversed

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Books that have resurfaced prove to be a fount of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek Muse of love poetry, and a muse is a source of inspiration.

clue.text: A number a lot may go for cheaply?

definitions.text: A number a lot may go for cheaply?

parts.words: A number a lot may go for cheaply?
parts.note: an auction lot sold very cheaply goes 'for a ...', and a ... is a musical number

explanation.surface: Wondering what price an auction lot fetches at a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go for a song' is an idiom for being sold very cheaply; a number is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a musical piece performed, the very thing an auction bargain proverbially goes for.

clue.text: Good fellow on the beer becoming overfamiliar

parts.note: ST is saint, a good man
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A decent chap who has taken to drink is wearing out his welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale jokes or ideas are tired from repetition, too familiar to interest anyone.

clue.text: Raising agent, heading off in this direction?

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter, the head of the word, is removed

parts.note: yeast is the agent that makes bread dough rise

explanation.surface: Bread's leavening heading away in a particular direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a hint that the direction is one particular compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four compass points, the direction of sunrise.

clue.text: Father's host for old TV show

parts.note: dad's is father's, with the apostrophe dropped
a host is a great number, especially an army

explanation.surface: A father's entertaining crowd is the subject of a vintage programme.
explanation.walkthrough: DAD'S ARMY is a classic British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard, a reserve of older men.
explanation.definitionFit: A much-repeated BBC comedy from the late 1960s and 1970s, so an old television programme.

clue.text: Detective having daughter carried out

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police rank

explanation.surface: An investigator whose daughter has been taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a task is to perform it, so did means performed or carried out.

clue.text: Road-edge spoiled, with battered corners

indicators.note: spoiled means damaged or messed up, so the letters are knocked into new order

explanation.surface: A damaged verge leaves a book with worn corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages with folded, worn corners look like a hound's floppy ears.

clue.text: Eagle sailors found in middle of Greece

indicators.note: found in says the sailors are discovered inside the other piece
middle of means the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, sailors collectively

explanation.surface: A bird of prey that seamen came across in central Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle, a crossword favourite, a big coastal bird of prey.
